policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere הַשְּׂבָכָה carries the article, the ketiv שבכה does not. The ASV's 'beside the network' supplies an English definite article that anaphoric reference to the network of v.17-18 would require under either reading, so the wording does not distinguish them; the qere base stands.
Qere וְקָו and ketiv וקוה are orthographic variants of the same noun קָו 'line', both rendered 'and a line'. Nothing in the ASV wording or its notes distinguishes them; the qere base stands.

The pair differs only in where the conjunction is written: qere וְעַל מִסְגְּרֹתֶיהָ against ketiv עַל וּמִסְגְּרֹתֶיהָ. Either yields the ASV's 'and on the panels thereof', so the wording does not distinguish them; the qere base stands.
Qere הָאֵלֶּה 'these' against ketiv האהל 'the tent'. The ASV reads 'even all these vessels', rendering the demonstrative and showing no trace of a tent, so it follows the qere.
